title: Functional repair: complete filling, renewed access and useful pressure loads
status_authority: Whole supplied source at its stated assumptions and read scopes; no Capital science execution, physical qualification or new independent audit.
reported_status: ROOT distinguishes actual pumped vascular fracture repair, bounded rapid-adhesion materials and pressure compensation from renewed useful actuator function. Introduced models show that a feed throat can seal before filling a defect and that small local deposits can dominate later access. A hypothetical pressure-body screen does not inherit tested actuator strength from tensile specimens. Earlier local-heating and observation results remain unchanged; no compatible autonomous repair material, mold, complete force-work cycle, renewal life or whole-cost advantage is supplied.

Earlier local-heating and observation results remain unchanged; no compatible autonomous repair material, mold, complete force-work cycle, renewal life or whole-cost advantage is supplied. Actual missing material, retained load, mixing, transport, cure, temporary support, useful force-displacement-work and renewed access belong to the complete operation. The hydraulic example assumes a rectangular throat and prescribed cure-front growth; the pressure screen assumes an undeformed isotropic thick cylinder. Neither constitutive law is a measured actuator or resin model.

proof_availability.classification_scope: Prepared epoxy fractures with pumping, support, manual cleanup, long cure or clamping are not autonomous soft actuators. Manually realigned tensile cuts and limited contact tests do not qualify a useful pressure body or repeated damaged-device life. External sealing, recovered shape or compensated force can coexist with missing material or depleted redundancy. All numerical laws below are introduced; no actual cure window, renewed conduit or restored useful-load life is established.
